in_hebrew.name: הילטרודה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: משמעות ארוכה: 'היל' - רכיב (מקור גרמני) 'טרודה' - נתן (מקור גרמני) פירוש: 'אלהים יתן' (מקור עברי). השם 'הילטרודה' הוא שם שכינוי, שמקורו במילה הגרמנית 'hiltra' שפירושה 'אלהים' והמילה 'trud' שפירושה 'נתן'.

in_greek.name: Ηιλτρουδά
in_greek.long_meaning: σημαίνετε: 'Ηιλτρουδά' είναι ονομασία που προέρχεται από την Γερμανική γλώσσα. Η λέξη 'Ηιλτρουδά' αποτελείται από δύο στοιχεία: 'Ηιλτρουδά' (Ηιλτρουδα) που σημαίνει 'θεός' και 'δίδωσι' (δίδωσι) που σημαίνει 'δίδωσι'.

in_latin.name: Hiltruda

in_english.name: Hiltruda
in_english.long_meaning: meaning: The name Hiltruda has Germanic roots and is composed of two elements: 'hil' meaning 'God' and 'trud' meaning 'gives'. In Christian tradition, the name Hiltruda is associated with the concept of divine providence and the idea that God provides for his people.

data.cultural_impact: The name Hiltruda may have been popular during the Germanic, European Middle Ages, where courage and battle skills were highly valued. Hiltruda may have been seen as a warrior-maiden or a counselor to her lord in battle, symbolizing wisdom and strength.
data.spiritual_significance: Religiously, Hiltruda can be seen as a protector and advisor in times of spiritual or emotional conflict. Her name signifies the power of seeking wise counsel, especially during times of tribulation or personal struggle. As a result, Hiltruda can be a reminder to turn to faith and prayer when facing difficult challenges.

historical_references.reference: Hiltruda, the daughter of Charlemagne, was the abbess of the double monastery of Chelles and Prémontré. She was born in 755 and became a nun at Chelles around 780. Hiltruda is known for her patronage of the arts, her generous donations to the monastery, and her role in the foundation of the double monastery of Prémontré. She ruled the monastery until her death around 828.

Legend has it that Hiltruda, the Frankish princess, was abducted by Vikings in 845 and held captive for several years. She was eventually ransomed by her brother, Charles II the Bald, and returned to France. Her experiences during her captivity influenced her later life and are said to have contributed to the growth of monasticism in the region.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Hiltruda is of Old High German origin, meaning 'battle-strength'. While it was popular during the Middle Ages, it is now mostly of interest to scholars and enthusiasts of European history, medieval studies, and Germanic mythology. Hiltruda is mentioned in various historical and mythological texts, such as the Nibelungenlied and the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle. Modern usage of the name can be found on academic research databases like JSTOR and Project MUSE for scholarly articles and theses, on Wikipedia for historical and mythological information, and on Goodreads for books related to the subject matter.
